observationsNotFindings: OBL-FX-AUTHORING is measured leftoverDesign true in two places at once — here on the DR-G09 gate, and on DR-105 where permission leftover-join.v7 measures it. As on the G19 chain, this is parallel recording rather than double-counting: the values agree, registerRowNote draws the row-versus-gate distinction explicitly, and the split is handled precisely where it matters. The doesNot entry names OBL-R10-AUTHORING, OBL-R6-AUTHORING, OBL-FC-C1 and OBL-BLK-1..4 as not stolen and deliberately omits OBL-FX-AUTHORING, which is the gate's own remainder. That omission is the correct one, and it is the detail that distinguishes a disciplined parallel record from a land grab.

The subject asserts a negative about its own basis — that G09 v3 has no leftoverNameNote — and I checked it rather than passing over it. Negative claims are the easiest thing to assert and the least likely to be tested, and this one carries weight: several joins in this family justify their own existence by pointing at a leftoverNameNote that reserved the work. Here the justification runs the other way, through leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded, and the absence it depends on is real.

This is the largest pin set I have measured in this sweep — sixteen path-bearing basedOn pins and seventeen recordedInputs entries, spanning two ROW joins, two GATE predecessors, a harness, a catalog and an input corpus — and none of it drifted, with every basedOn path also present in recordedInputs. A chain this wide is where a stale pin would ordinarily surface.

The R-10/R-6 separation is structural rather than rhetorical. The fourteen FX classes and the two race byte-sets live in different top-level keys, both matching live G09 v3 by ==, so the fold the dispatch forbids would require moving a member between keys rather than merely rewording a sentence. That makes the prohibition cheap to verify and hard to violate accidentally.

The GATE chain is single-reviewer throughout. Codex verdicts do exist earlier in the permission ROW chain, at permission-leftover-join v1 and v2, but no Codex artifact exists for this gate join at any version or for anything this subject pins.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. Both register checks pass by == against a DR-G09 row parsed into all eight cells before the subject was opened: liveGateOwners.DR-G09 is 'Security', matching the live owner cell and the pinned harness, and file08StatusToken is OPEN. The R-10/R-6 fold prohibition is honoured structurally rather than rhetorically — the fourteen FX classes and the two race byte-sets sit in separate top-level keys, both equal to live G09 v3 by ==, the fourteen list contains no R- token, and OBL-FX-AUTHORING's own list is identical to it. The DR-105 non-theft claim was resolved against live files, not summaries: permission leftover-join.v7's leftoverDesign-true set is exactly the eight named, and G09 v3's leftoverDesignRemainingOnDR105 is that same eight-member list. The v6-versus-v7 distinction is real — v6 has no OBL-R10-R6-INPUT-CORPUS and v7 does — so the two INPUT obligations rest on the right joins. I checked the subject's negative claim that G09 v3 has no leftoverNameNote, since its account of why it is the GATE leftover-join depends on that absence, and a recursive search confirms it. Both predecessor roles were checked against the predecessors' actual obligation tables, because that same template slot landed a SHOULD-FIX on the G23 chain this session; here 'named-catalog' is legitimate, since G09 genuinely has a catalog artifact and v1 genuinely carries OBL-G09-NAMED-CATALOG, and predecessorV2's 'This v3 does not reuse the v2 version number' names the correct version. Sixteen basedOn pins and seventeen recordedInputs all recompute, all seven cited verdicts are genuinely ACCEPT 0/0, all ten envelope mentions and all wall-clock mentions are denials, and no bare integer could be read as an expiry age or cleanup bound. OBL-FX-AUTHORING is recorded true on both the gate and the row; that is disclosed parallel recording, and the not-stolen list correctly omits it. 20 attacks run, 20 refuted.
